Photograph: Reuters First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Anger after Trump’s secret flight swap appears to offer up staff and media as decoys Democrats demand congressional briefing after passenger-laden Air Force One sent on decoy flight despite security scare. Plus, the 11 biggest wellness trends of 2026 so far Martin Belam Wed 12 Aug 2026 07.46 EDT Last modified on Wed 12 Aug 2026 08.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. Democrats have called for a congressional briefing after a charade in which Donald Trump was secretly spirited into a different plane than the one the public and press believed he was travelling on. When US intelligence allegedly found a credible threat that Iran plotted to kill the president last month, Trump left Air Force One in a catering truck. More than a hundred aides, officials and reporters were kept onboard to fly towards Britain from Turkey, without being told there was a threat to their lives. “It appears that the idea was we can reduce the danger to President Trump by offering up 100 or so people to be killed by the Iranians in his place,” said Steven Cash, the executive director of the non-profit Steady State who is a former CIA intelligence officer and senior adviser to the Department of Homeland Security’s intelligence branch. How did the plot to smuggle Trump off the plane unfold? In this video , the Guardian breaks down the footage from that day, showing how the president reportedly boarded the old Air Force One jet in view of television cameras, and then was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies before flight. David Crowley defeats Francesca Hong to win Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor View image in fullscreen David Crowley, pictured with Karen Hilt, left, pulled off a last-minute victory after re-entering the race. Photograph: Kayla Wolf/AP David Crowley, a Milwaukee county executive, pulled off a last-minute victory after re-entering the Wisconsin governor’s race and defeating Francesca Hong. Hong, a chef and former restaurant owner from Madison, ran on a platform that included free childcare up to 400% of the federal poverty level, free school meals and a one-year moratorium on the construction of new datacenters, which differentiated her from her Democratic colleagues in the governor’s race. Where have progressives enjoyed electoral success this week? Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s lieutenant governor, won her Democratic primary for US Senate in a race centered on immigration enforcement. Flanagan, who beat the congresswoman Angie Craig, recently told the Guardian: “So often I think Democrats are like: ‘What do we think we can win?’ Instead of: ‘What are the fights that we should be picking?’” What happened in South Carolina’s abbreviated special Republican primary? Darline Graham, appointed to complete the Senate term of her late brother, Lindsey, will face the congressman Ralph Norman in a runoff on 25 August. The winner will face the Democratic nominee Annie Andrews in November’s midterms. Judge blocks Trump’s order aimed at using USPS to restrict mail-in voting View image in fullscreen The ruling expands on an ‌earlier order preventing the mail-in voting changes being implemented in 23 mostly Democratic-led states. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images A federal judge on Tuesday blocked ⁠the US Postal ⁠Service ​from implementing part of Donald Trump’s executive order that aims ⁠to tighten rules for mail-in voting before November’s midterm elections. The ruling expanded on an ‌earlier order that had prevented Trump’s administration from implementing it in 23 mostly Democratic-led states. Where else are Trump policies facing a new legal challenge? The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and other advocacy groups have asked a federal judge to block Donald Trump from enforcing his latest attempt to restrict eligibility ​for birthright citizenship. The supreme court previously said Trump’s original executive order, which he issued the day he began ⁠his second term in the White House, violated the 14th amendment to the US constitution. ICE to spend up to $20m on gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks View image in fullscreen The gloves being ordered for ICE agents have previously been used in settings such as jails in the US. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/AP ICE plans to spend up to $20m to purchase thousands of gloves for officers and agents that can deliver painful electric shocks , according to a notice published Monday by the Department of Homeland Security. The devices, called Glove (generated low output voltage emitter), are manufactured by Compliant Technologies of Lexington, Kentucky. According to the manufacturer: “The discomfort associated with the stimulation is usually effective in bringing individuals into compliance in less than three seconds and leaves no burns, marks or scars.” It has advertised the device as a “humane, low-optics, de-escalation solution for many situations facing our men and women in uniform.” The gloves have previously been used in settings such as jails in the US. In other news … View image in fullscreen Rescuers and volunteers search for survivors in Cali, Colombia. At at least 240 people have been killed and 3,000 missing after the quake. Photograph: Joaquín Sarmiento/AFP/Getty Images Colombian rescue workers are racing to find survivors after the country’s deadliest earthquake this century killed at least 240 people and left at least 3,000 missing. Firefighters and residents of south Lebanon have accused the Israeli military of lighting wildfires in the region , as forested areas burned down in blazes sparked by Israeli bombing. Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that the governing body Fifa has adopted under his presidency. The Bumble dating app said it was dropping its women-first messaging rule ⁠that has ⁠been ​a defining feature since its launch in 2014. Stat of the day: Samuel Alito gained up to $2.9m from oil and gas assets since joining supreme court View image in fullscreen There are calls for Samuel Alito to recuse himself from a climate accountability case involving oil and gas firms. Photograph: Vincenzo Livieri/Reuters Critics argue the US high court justice should recuse himself from an upcoming climate accountability case involving fossil fuel firms after a review of financial disclosures showed Samuel Alito gained up to $2.9m from his oil and gas interests between 2005 and 2024. Well Actually: The 11 biggest wellness trends of 2026 so far View image in fullscreen Wellness trends are sometimes legitimate, sometimes utter nonsense, but can often be somewhere in between. Composite: The Guardian/Getty Images Every year, the wellness industry churns out new products and practices. Sometimes, these trends are legitimate. Sometimes they’re utter nonsense. Often they’re somewhere in between. Madeleine Aggeler lists the wellness trends that have provoked controversy and interest in 2026. Don’t miss this: Drowned the day her visa came through – the tragedy of a Moroccan footballer trying to reach Ceuta View image in fullscreen Faten Ben Omar El Azizi was among at least 141 people who died during last month’s mass crossing to the Spanish territory in north Africa. Faten Ben Omar El Azizi was among at least 141 people who died during last month’s mass crossing to the Spanish territory in north Africa. In the cruellest of ironies, on the day she drowned her mother was told that the footballer had just been granted a visa to go to Spain. This is their story . Climate check: Europe is the world’s fastest warming continent. What is to blame? View image in fullscreen The wreckage of a German warship emerges from the Danube in Serbia, as water levels fall during prolonged hot and dry weather. Photograph: Andrej Isaković/AFP/Getty Images The climate crisis is hitting Europe hard in 2026, warming twice as fast as any other continent – and the consequences are deadly. The Guardian’s environment editor, Damian Carrington, explains the multiple factors behind it . Photograph: Robert F Bukaty/AP Rather him than me – a Maumelle high school student felt unusual movement inside his headgear after warmups last week and discovered a slithering 2ft venomous cottonmouth . https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-green.text: LONDON — Green Party Leader Zack Polanski announced Thursday he wants to stand as a candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election to succeed Keir Starmer. Polanski, who took over the left-wing party last year, told the Camden New Journal he hopes to represent the Greens in the central London contest — a shot across Labour’s bows in what has previously been considered a safe seat for the governing party. “I have lived and worked in this community over many years, I know it well and I love it,” the Green leader said. “It represents so many of the things that make London so special. I am so excited by the prospect of representing this place in Parliament.” Advertisement Advertisement Starmer stood down from the House of Commons this week, saying he wanted to devote more attention to international affairs. He quit as prime minister earlier this year after losing support in his own party, and has been succeeded by Andy Burnham. No date has yet been set for the contest. Polanski will still need to be selected by local Green Party members. That selection is expected to take place next week. In a taste of his campaign pitch, Polanski said “voters will have someone who will always fight their corner — never scared of big donors or the party whip.” And he charged: “Too often Labour has stood up for corporations and big money. I will stand up for people struggling to pay their bills.” Polanski has overseen a boost to the Green Party membership and led his party to a strong performance at the local elections in May, but has faced scrutiny around the vetting of candidates and his social media posts. He has been a member of the London Assembly scrutinizing Mayor Sadiq Khan since 2021. Starmer held the Holborn and St Pancras seat in 2024 with an 11,572 majority, but faced a strong challenge from a left-wing independent and the Greens. Advertisement Advertisement

https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/03/karp.text: Menü Kereső Az ukrán parlament határozattal ítélte el a kárpátaljai magyarokkal szembeni szovjet atrocitásokat Külföld Weiler Vilmos Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A második világháború alatt és után a kárpátaljai magyarokkal szemben elkövetett atrocitásokat elítélő nyilatkozatot fogadott el az ukrán parlament – számolt be róla az Ukrajnai Magyar Demokrata Szövetség . A nyilatkozat fontos gesztus Magyarország felé, amely továbbra is blokkolja Ukrajna uniós csatlakozásának folyamatát . A nyilatkozat elfogadása mellett az ukrán parlamentben – amelyet hivatalosan Ukrajnai Legfelsőbb Tanácsnak hívnak – 261-en voksoltak, nulla nem és nulla tartózkodás született. A nyilatkozattal Ukrajna hivatalosan elismeri és elítéli az 1944 és 1946 között a szovjet katonai közigazgatás által Kárpátalján elkövetett bűncselekményeket. A nyilatkozat szövege szerint „az Ukrajnai Legfelsőbb Tanács kifejezi elvi álláspontját azokkal, az 1944–1946-os években Kárpátalján történt tragikus eseményekkel kapcsolatban, amelyek a szovjet katonai közigazgatás létrehozásához és a régió későbbi kényszerű szovjetizálásához kapcsolódnak. 1944 őszén, a magyar és német csapatok visszavonulása után Kárpátalja területe azonnal a szovjet katonai közigazgatás ellenőrzése alá került. Ebben az időben a szovjet katonai közigazgatás az NKVD és a SMERS szervei és tisztviselői közreműködésével az úgynevezett munkatáborokba való mozgósítás ürügyével tömeges, jogellenes letartóztatásokat hajtott végre a 18 és 50 év közötti kárpátaljai civil férfilakosság körében. Kárpátalja több ezer békés lakosát bírósági ítélet nélkül deportálták a GULAG-rendszer koncentrációs táboraiba.” A nyilatkozat szerint Ukrajna „mint a jogállamiságot elismerő és a totalitarizmus minden megnyilvánulását elítélő demokratikus állam, kötelességének tartja hivatalosan elismerni a szovjet katonai közigazgatás által a magyar nemzetiségű polgári lakosság ellen 1944 és 1946 között elkövetett tömeges elnyomás tényét, az úgynevezett » malenykij robotot « , valamint a Kárpátalja német nemzetiségű lakossága ellen elkövetett elnyomást, mint a kommunista totalitárius rezsim által elkövetett bűncselekményeket.” A nyilatkozat szerint Ukrajna ezenkívül erkölcsi kötelességének tekinti, hogy a kárpátaljai szovjet elnyomás áldozatainak tiszteletére emléktáblákat helyezzenek ki, tudományos kutatásokat szervezzenek, és oktatási programokat valósítsanak meg. Szintén ígéretet tesznek arra, hogy az ezzel kapcsolatos levéltári anyagokat nyilvánosságra fogják hozni – írja az ukrán Pravda . Éppen csütörtökön derült ki , hogy Ukrajna uniós csatlakozási folyamata azért akadt meg, mert Magyarország továbbra is blokkolja a 2. és 3. tárgyalási klaszterek átvilágítási jelentéseit. Orbán Anita külügyminiszter erről azt mondta: Ukrajna gyorsított felvételét semmilyen körülmények között nem támogatják, és most azt várják, hogy az ukránok hajtsák végre a júniusban megtárgyalt kisebbségi megállapodást .
